title: Interfacial & Nonequilibrium Physics
subtitle: Molecular interfaces, defects & ionic dynamics
question: How do molecular-scale interfaces and defects reshape electronic and ionic energy landscapes?
whatIControl: Molecular contacts · thin-film interfaces · defect environments
whatIMeasure: Charge transport · trap behavior · state-formation dynamics
whyItMatters: Interfacial physics links material chemistry to device behavior and reliability.
summary: Molecular contacts and local defects set the conditions for transport. I connect interface engineering in optoelectronics with trap control and ionic dynamics in emerging memory.
motivation: An electronic device is often governed by a small fraction of its material: the interface, the defect, or the pathway an ion can access. Understanding these local environments offers a route from chemical structure to device function.
current: Current work investigates state-formation dynamics and low-frequency noise to study the precision limits of ion-migration-controlled multilevel memristors. This is an active research question, with outcomes still to be established.
results: Published work spans SAM-based hole-selective contacts, intermediate-layer-assisted trap reduction, and hydrogen-bond-driven artificial synapses.
future: Connect metastable states, stochastic switching, and electrical noise to a more predictive description of ionic memory. RTN-specific analysis and atomistic modeling remain directions to develop.
homeDescription: How molecular interfaces, defects, and ionic dynamics govern transport across electronic devices.
